correctness.rationale: Funk–Hecke with normalized sphere measure gives each harmonic-channel 2x2 multiplier M_l with phi_l(z)=2^nu Gamma(nu+1) z^{-nu} J_{l+nu}(z). On 0<bv<j_{nu,1}, the positive Bessel product and monotonicity of its first zero make ratio phi_l(at)/phi_l(bt) strictly increasing in t; det M_l<0 for u<v. Single observation sphere always has a nontrivial 1x2 null vector. The Bessel series cancels determinant leading terms and gives -kappa_l^2(abuv)^l (b²-a²)(v²-u²)/[4(l+nu+1)](1+O(1/l)). Bottom-right entry asymptotically dominates, and sigma_min=abs(det)/sigma_max gives stated sharp ill-conditioning. Independent 90-digit Bessel evaluations for d=2,3,5 and degrees 0,1,5,40 checked determinant sign and determinant/leading-term ratios 0.9966, 0.9931, 0.9896 at degree 40. All-l uniqueness rests on the proof, not finite samples.

evidence: General Bessel products and harmonic decompositions are established; they imply strict sign after the new two-radius comparison.

evidence: Both primary theorems explicitly assume source measure is supported on one sphere and make only injectivity conclusions; the new result has two independently varying densities plus a quantitative singular-value law.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Combining two copies of a one-shell uniqueness theorem does NOT separate two summands measured only through their sum; the 2x2 determinant proof is needed.
